chunks: 1965 - Ibn Muskan narrated from Al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the salat (prayer) in the month of Ramadan, so he said:

“Thirteen rakʿahs, including al-Witr and the two rakʿahs of al-Ṣubḥ before dawn. Thus the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to pray, and I likewise pray. If there had been something better, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله would not have left it.”

key_terms.ثَلَاثَ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً: thirteen units of prayer specified by the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله whose practice is cited as proof
key_terms.رَكْعَتَا ٱلصُّبْحِ: the two rakʿahs associated with the dawn prayer before Fajr
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the time in which this prayer practice is discussed
key_terms.قَبْلَ ٱلْفَجْرِ: before daybreak, clarifying the time of the two rakʿahs
key_terms.يُصَلِّي: used to pray, indicating established prophetic practice
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةِ: the ritual salat (prayer) being asked about in Ramadan
key_terms.ٱلْوَتْرُ: the Witr prayer included within the total count

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام describe the salat (prayer) in the month of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith states the number of recommended prayers in the month of Ramadan as thirteen rakʿahs, including al-Witr and the two rakʿahs before Fajr. The Imam عليه السلام grounds this practice in the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and presents it as the preferred form of worship.
